articleTitle: An Investigation into Able Students' Understanding of Motion Graphs
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: This paper reports on three tasks that were used to evaluate the understanding that able 13-year-old mathematics students have of motion graphs. The results indicted that relatively few students had a sound understanding that could be applied consistently. The major error that was demonstrated by the students was the use of a position criterion to draw conclusions about speeds. The tasks also revealed that there were a number of students who were unfamiliar with velocity. A number of questions that formed part of the tasks contained interesting features that seemed to prompt changes in reasoning for some students. The authors feel that these questions could be worthy of further investigation in order to develop strategies for improving student understanding.

articleTitle: The SUMSMAN Project and its Implications for Computer-Based Assessment
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: Since 1996, four high-speed computer links (Metropolitan Area Networks, or MANs) have been available to Scottish Higher Education Institutions for use in teaching and learning. To stimulate innovative use of the MANs, The Scottish Higher Education Funding Council (SHEFC) supported a small number of subject-based projects within Phase 2 of its Use of the MANs Initiative (UMI2). The outcomes of one of these projects, Scottish Universities Mathematics and Statistics across the MANs (SUMSMAN), will be described, with particular emphasis on the implementation of computer-based assessment in mathematics and statistics.

publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: The gear system of a mountain bike is examined to discover any redundancy in the many gear settings available to the cyclist. A best strategy for changing up through the gears is suggested for a typical 21-gear system and also an adjustment to the available gears is suggested that would result in a smoother change.

articleTitle: Open Testing with a Large Databank of Multiple Choice Questions
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: Sharing test questions is now a real possibility using a system called TAL (Test and Learn). The potentially huge number of questions in a national database offers the opportunity for open testing where each student has “his own” test and so can take the test in his own time, saving on supervision and PCs.

articleTitle: A Residual Mathematical Core for the Incorporated Engineer
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: SARTOR3 highlights the importance of mathematics to the Incorporated Engineer. This paper has described the recommendations of an IMA working group on the appropriate mathematical formation of Incorporated Engineers. It has outlined the principles that led to these recommendations and described the consultation with engineering institutions that has taken place to ensure that a realistic, relevant and worthwhile mathematical experience is set in place for would-be Incorporated Engineers. The role of technology has been highlighted as fundamental in the education and professional practice of Incorporated Engineers. The working group believes that its guidelines can be used as a benchmark by those designing mathematics curricula for engineers under the new regime.

publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: An example of the modelling power of Mathematics, demonstrated in a piece of A-Level student course work, was undertaken as part of the MEI Structured Mathematics scheme. A system of two “masses” and two springs oscillating in one dimension is found to be accurately modelled by a system of linear differential equations. An ultrasound motion sensor and electronic datalogging system enable an effective comparison of model and reality.

articleTitle: Core Geometrical Knowledge for using the Modelling Power of Geometry with Cabri-Geometry
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: Euclidean geometry has disappeared from some curricula at secondary school and university. This situation may change in the next few years. The power of geometry as a modelling tool, which allows a global representation of a system, is deeply reinforced by the availability of software packages of dynamic geometry such as like Cabri-géomètre. Such open-ended environments offer a large range of geometrical tools for creating dynamic geometrical figures which can be fully animated.

abstract: This article is concerned with how bookmakers calculate the betting odds on each of the horses in a race. It shows how an understanding of probability theory is necessary if bookmakers are to maximise their profit. It also shows that the only winners, when it comes to gambling, are the bookmakers

articleTitle: Experiences and Observations on the Introduction of Concept Questions into a Mechanics Module
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: In this paper we reflect on the introduction of concept questions into examination papers in mechanics. The research shows that student attainment on the concept type questions compares favourably with their performance on more traditional questions.

publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: This paper summarises the authors' recent research into patterns of Internet use in schools, providing a detailed picture which suggests that, in the majority of schools, the use of the Internet is at a very early and restricted level of use. These findings are used to support a critical review of the types of resources currently available via the Internet and their usefulness for teaching in schools. Types of educational content provider are considered and exemplification is drawn from sites relevant to Mathematics teachers. Looking to the future, the paper reflects on the communication aspects of the Internet and on the Web-based resources that teachers need and which the National Grid for Learning should support. Ways of filling identified gaps are also considered.

articleTitle: Extreme Value Analysis as Exemplified by a Milk Carton: An Actual Problem from the Real World of Mass Production
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: The everyday one-litre milk carton with its square base area is examined for an optimum, i.e. minimum, use of material. The actual conditions of milk carton production are looked at, including the adhesive edges, etc. The dimensions of the one-litre carton and the half-litre carton are subsequently found to lie very close to their optimum values. A procedure for the joint optimization of both packs leads to surprising results. This case study can be incorporated into an analysis course as a typical optimum-value problem.

publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: In this article a comparison is undertaken of the examination performance of mathematics under-graduates with respect to the style of A-level taken. In particular, groups taking modular A-levels have been compared in several respects with those sitting the non-modular version. For the most recent year of entry the modular group performed better by and large, reversing the pattern of the previous two years' entries. Female students perform better in almost all respects.

articleTitle: The Emerging Philosophy behind Computer-Based Assessment
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: The computer can play a role in several forms of assessment: diagnostic and self-testing, continuous and grading assessment. Automatic marking has many benefits for the human teacher: it is objective, fast, accurate, flexible and robust. The best test engines expect students to input mathematical expressions as answers, much as in a written examination. Over the last decade, many HCI issues in mathematical assessment by computer have been resolved. Students highlight as important the issue of partial credit if the computer is to grade their work fairly. This paper concentrates on the educational aspects of an assessment engine for mathematics.

abstract: The basic mechanics of cycling is investigated with a simple reckoning of how much effort is needed from the cyclist. The work done by the cyclist is quantified when the ride is on the flat and also when pedalling uphill. It is shown that by making use of the available gears on, say, a mountain bike, cycling uphill can be accomplished without pain.

publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: Formative assessment, where students hand in work that tutors return annotated with comments, has been a casualty of the increased pressures on academic staff time. However, this is a valuable part of the learning experience. This paper describes how computer-aided assessment (CAA) can provide a means of preserving formative assessment within the curriculum at a fraction of the time–cost involved with written work. CAA no longer means only multiple choice. Sophisticated, yet easy to use, software packages like Question Mark Designer permit a variety of assessment styles. This paper illustrates some of the styles available.

articleTitle: Deal Shuffles with an Eight-Card Deck and a Stella Octangula
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: The invariants of the actions of a class of shuffles on an eight-card deck are investigated by recognising that the group of such shuffles is isomorphic to a subgroup of the symmetry group of a geometric object called a stella octangula. This isomorphism is used to gain insight into how certain card “tricks” are natural consequences of the shuffles.

articleTitle: Buffon's Needle Problem with a Twist
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: Some simple variations of Buffon's well-known needle problem in probability are discussed, and an interesting observation connecting the corresponding results is then made.

articleTitle: Essential Mathematical Concepts Needed by Users of Computer Algebra
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: Computer algebra systems have great potential for professional engineers, scientists and technologists. They can reduce the tedium of routine manipulation required in some mathematical models and procedures, give a greater assurance of accuracy, and even enable users to apply techniques which they might find difficult without such assistance. But learning the basic concepts, particularly of the more sophisticated and capable computer algebra systems, is itself a mathematical activity. For instance, the formal concepts of functions must be grasped very clearly if the user is to get the best from these systems. This paper will explore those theoretical concepts, which may be seen as essential enabling skills for users of computer algebra systems.

articleTitle: Algebra and Symbol Sense in the Formation of Engineers
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of the educational reforms of the 1980s and 90s, which resulted in a decreasing emphasis on teaching and learning algebra in schools. The argument is made that too much focus on individual learning tends to ignore the mathematical cognitive tools which are the cultural heritage of practising engineers. A consideration of the role and potential of computer environments also points to a concern with a focus on the individual as opposed to the social and cultural aspects of learning.

publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: Geometric representations of the Pythagorean theorem usually merely relate three different squares whose sides are the sides of a common right triangle. A perhaps more visually revealing image is presented that demonstrates the theorem, a<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> + b<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> + c<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, using a single common area. This representation is a stronger illustration for students, allowing them a visual insight into the correctness of this ancient theorem.

articleTitle: How Far should the Residual Core of Mathematics be affected by the Computer?
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: Advocates of the increasing use of the computer in the teaching and learning of mathematics claim that certain topics and techniques need no longer be taught because the ready availability of the computer has rendered them obsolete. At the same time, there has been a reduction in the mathematics syllabus at all levels, leading to calls from many quarters that this trend has gone too far and must be reversed. How far should the access to so much computer power influence the core of mathematics which needs teaching at different levels? This paper addresses that question.

publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: Air resistance is essential to a safe parachute jump. Without air resistance the jumper's velocity would increase without bound. In this paper we present a simple differential equation model, which can be analysed using A-level calculus techniques, of the freefall phase of a parachute jump. Hie predictions of this model are compared with data taken from the parachuting literature. We show how the model can be modified to allow an investigation of the effect of the mass of the jumper on the distance fallen during the freefall phase

articleTitle: Mathematics Around the World: A Look at Mathematics in the International Baccalaureate
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: The International Baccalaureate Organisation provides educational programs in over 800 schools throughout the world. The Diploma Programme is offered to students in the last two years of high school, that is whose ages range from 17 to 19 years approximately. There are four mathematics subjects offered in the programme, and these are offered as either standard level courses of 150 hours or higher level courses of 240 hours over the two-year period. It is assumed that all students have access to a graphic display calculator throughout these programmes. Assessment is made up of two major components. The internal assessment component consists of assignments or projects and external assessment consisting of two examinations of varying length depending on the course of study followed.

articleTitle: A Lesson on Double Packable Solids
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: A double packable solid is a convex polyhedron, copies of which can pack space, and such that there is a way of laying out its surface so that copies of this pack the plane. This paper discusses the existence of various double packable solids. Double packable solids play a role in the design of efficient product packaging.

articleTitle: Modelling Traffic Flow: Solving and Interpreting Differential Equations
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: A simple mathematical model for how traffic flows along a road is introduced. The resulting first-order ordinary differential equations can be used as an application of solution techniques taught at A-level and first year undergraduate level, and as a motivator to encourage students to think critically about the physical interpretation of the results which the equation produces.

articleTitle: Micromaths: The Planets Suite: 1st Movement: Theory (Allegro)
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: This paper considers an approach to addressing the decline in the level of achievement of British pupils in mathematics. It looks in detail at the differences between the teaching methods of Britain and Hungary, as research studies have indicated the high level of achievement of Hungarian pupils in mathematics. The paper outlines three theoretical perspectives (radical constructivism, social constructivism and Vygotsky's zone of proximal development) that are helpful in considering the important differences. The major differences are considered under four categories: expectation and consistency, assessment, continuity and differentiated teaching. The paper proposes the method of whole-class interactive teaching as a way forward that would improve pupils' achievement, and gives practical suggestions for developing such a teaching strategy.

articleTitle: What Does the WWW Offer Mathematics Students and Teachers
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: A brief historical sketch of the World Wide Web (WWW) explains why browsers are needed and what they can do for mathematics teachers and students. We compare information available on the Web for mathematics with an encyclopaedia and with books, say why the Web offers something vital and different and contrast the Web with book-based information. Several examples of useful Web addresses (URLs) are included as illustrations. Finally, we look at presenting mathematical equations on Web pages.
